correctness.rationale: For common squared root norm 2, the unique smallest enclosing sphere is centered at the nearest point of the root convex hull to the origin. The two-step graph quotient has exactly the feasible margin triangle x>=0,y>=0,x+y<=1. Strictly convex quadratic minimization yields the center and radius, including strict positivity on the active boundary. Direct inner-product differences establish all and only the stated contact vertices and the 2h(theta-1) clearance. A standalone checker compares independently optimized nearest points for 441 instances, not as substitute for proof.

value.rationale: An infinite four-parameter natural two-step Ferrers graph family gains a complete, nontrivial Euclidean circumradius and exact contact classification. The Hall-type threshold separates uniform-marginal and constrained regimes, with a sharp quadratic radius loss and a strictly screened orbit of vertices. This finite graph pattern is a motivated structural boundary, not an arbitrary numerical example.
